why: Details the specific statistical volume requirements for valid A/B split testing (e.g., 40,000 sessions per variant) and explains how cross-channel traffic contamination invalidates test results.
topics: [sample size and power, stopping rules, common invalidations]

Topics. sample size and power / the math required for statistical significance: needing roughly 1,000 conversions per variant to trust a 10-20% conversion lift, which at a 2.5% conversion rate requires 40,000 sessions per variant (80,000 total sessions). stopping rules / the error of ending tests prematurely the moment they show a positive result (false positives) rather than letting them run for the full duration (e.g., 1-4 weeks) required for statistical relevancy. common invalidations / cross-channel contamination (e.g., Klaviyo email traffic hitting the test pages simultaneously), software routing errors, and the extended time-to-purchase factor (e.g., the average Meta user takes 1.5 clicks to convert).

Look for. The specific traffic threshold math: 1,000 conversions per variant = 40,000 sessions at a 2.5% CR = 80,000 total sessions required for a valid split test. The rule that tests must run on custom landing pages with isolated cold traffic (e.g., Meta only) to avoid contamination from email/warm channels. The common invalidation of "peeking": checking tests daily and stopping them immediately when a false positive appears.

Skip. The extensive landing page design teardowns (e.g., above-the-fold layout, answering 4 questions, checkout friction, copy principles) as this belongs entirely in 07-LPG.
